Fires once, when a job ends in failure — the training run itself broke (out of VRAM, an unusable dataset, a worker crash), so no adapter exists. Cancelling a job does NOT fire this: a cancel is user-initiated and recorded as `cancelled`, and the person who asked for it already has the answer. Same timing as `job.succeeded` — it fires on the next read of the job's state, and for a remote job only on a detail fetch. `error` is the worker's own message when it gave one, otherwise null.

Fires when POST /api/clips/start has actually begun a capture on Shadow and a clip id exists. A start Shadow refused, or one that never reached it (the fail-soft `{ available: false }` body), does not fire. The clip has no video and no duration yet — those arrive with `clip.ready`; this is the moment to react to recording having begun (announce it, arm a timer, dim a surface).

Fires when a fine-tune job has actually been accepted and a job id exists — either the local Unsloth worker returned one from POST /api/finetune/start, or a remote GPU node did. A start the GPU gate refused (no CUDA device on this node) or one the worker never accepted does not fire. Nothing is trained yet: the adapter arrives with `job.succeeded`. `target` says where it runs; dispatching to a remote node also starts the job on that node, so that node raises its own `job.started` against its own record — two Cores, two job ids, not a duplicate.

Fires when a recipe finished replaying against the native desktop without erroring. Carries ghost's structured run result (per-step success/timing), which is the only place that detail exists — nothing persists a run record. Fires once per replay, so a recipe run on a schedule fires on every run.

Fires when a replay could not complete: ghost is unreachable, the recipe is missing, or a step's target could not be found on screen. `error` is the same message the caller received. A replay raises either this or `replay.ended`, never both.

Keys 1 to 16 are the two button rows, top row first, then Solo/Arm, Mute/Select, the small logo button (Function), Page Up and Down, Track Left and Right, Record, Play and Shift. The encoder rows are dials 1 to 8, 9 to 16 and 17 to 24, top to bottom, and turn step by step; the faders are dials 25 to 32, and moving one turns its dial by how far it moved, from where it was first touched. Each button glows in its key's exact colour and each encoder's light takes its dial colour; Shift and the logo button have none, and the faders have no lights.

Keys 1 to 8 are the buttons and key 9 is Shift; the Page, Track, Function and Mode buttons are not keys. The encoder rows are dials 1 to 8 and 9 to 16 and turn step by step. Each button glows in its key's exact colour and each encoder's light takes its dial colour; Shift has none.

Keys 54 to 86 are track select, Master, activator, solo and arm, only on or off; Shift (87) and the foot pedal (88) have no light. Dials 1 to 8 are the channel faders, 9 the master fader and 10 Cue; a fader turns its dial by how far it moved, whichever slider mode the APC20 is in.

Keys 55 to 102 are track select, Master, activator, solo, arm, the device buttons, Pan, the sends and the transport buttons, only on or off; Stop All Clips, the arrows, Shift, Tap Tempo, Nudge and the two footswitches have no light. Dials 1 to 8 are the track knobs, 9 to 16 the device knobs, 17 Cue, 18 to 25 the channel faders, 26 the master fader and 27 the crossfader; a fader turns its dial by how far it moved, and the knob rings stay off.

Ryu Passport drawn as a cabinet of keys: each box holds one connection's sign-in, a session of at most {maxStateKib} KiB sealed with its tenant's own key and bound to its box, so a copy moved elsewhere will not open. One key leaves its box and Passport carries it to the site itself; only the fetched page comes back down to the agent's tray, with any echoed credential blacked out, so the agent never holds the key. A health sweep runs hourly and sends a missing or stale session back to needs sign-in. {failureLimit} unknown tokens from one address within {failureWindowSeconds} seconds are refused with {lockoutStatus}, the block doubling up to {maxBlockMinutes} minutes. The motion is a simulation, shown slower than a real fetch; the other keys are decoration.

Ryu Passport is an encrypted identity vault for agents. It keeps the sessions your agents are allowed to use, makes the upstream fetch itself, and redacts any credential echoed back, so only content reaches the agent.

Ryu cannot program the keyboard. In PrehKeyTec's own tool (WinProgrammer or MapMyKey), give each key you want here its own POSKey macro, POSKey001 to POSKey128, and turn on the OPOS/JavaPOS POSKey HID output; until then its keys reach Ryu as nothing. Each key is named by its POSKey number, counted from the bottom-left key. Ryu reads only that POSKey channel, so the keyboard keeps typing as usual, and it asks the keyboard which model it is when it is plugged in. There are no screens, lights or brightness to set.

Ryu drives the Launchpad through its MIDI port, so close Ableton Live, Novation Automap and other MIDI apps that use it first; on Windows only one app can hold the port, and elsewhere one sharing it draws over Ryu's lights. Web crawling and content extraction via the local Spider CLI (https://spider.cloud), declared as a command tool with no API key. Core runs the CLI behind a per-call loopback egress proxy that screens and IP-pins every connection the crawler opens, refusing private, loopback, link-local and cloud-metadata targets and ports other than 80 and 443.
Web fonts (.woff, .woff2) are not supported. Import the .ttf or .otf file.

Web search and content extraction via Parallel (https://parallel.ai), exposed as three HTTP tool runnables plus one capability adapter. Provides the swappable `web.search` and `web.extract` layers, so selecting it in the layer picker re-points the stable `web.search` / `web.extract` tools at Parallel without changing what agents call. Search works without a key through Parallel's public Search MCP endpoint; a BYOK Parallel API key unlocks the higher-limit REST API and extraction.

Web search and page fetch via the DeepSeek Search / Fetch API (https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/search), powered by DeepSeek's in-house search engine and exposed as two declarative HTTP tools. Provides the swappable `web.search` and `web.extract` layers, so selecting it in the layer picker re-points the stable `web.search` / `web.extract` tools at DeepSeek without changing what agents call. Billed per successful request; requires a BYOK DeepSeek API key.

Web search and page scraping via the Firecrawl v2 API (https://firecrawl.dev), exposed as two declarative HTTP tools. Provides the swappable `web.search` and `web.extract` layers, so selecting it in the layer picker re-points the stable `web.search` / `web.extract` tools at Firecrawl without changing what agents call. Requires a BYOK Firecrawl API key.
